reason: No on the unresolved T24 conflict and the drafter-as-reviewer arrangement, not on the goal. The Clerk drafted the bill, the sponsor authored Act 17, and the red-team shares the substrate; §2.3(3) then makes the Clerk the default independent reviewer of the legacy marker even though the Clerk drafted the bill and misread the checker once. That is not independent of the drafter and leaves the central containment as self-review. In addition, §2.4 retrospectively declares the 2026-10-23 filings an operational irregularity rather than a statutory breach while relying on a six-hour interval that §2.1 says creates no cycle identity; the prior legislative determination treated the second filing as a same-cycle attempt. The House can define the cycle prospectively, but this historical exoneration is not supported by an independent process. Act 22 is outside pilot scope, so the missing predictions are not the primary bar, but §7a has no probabilities and no calibration. If the marker reviewer were the Judiciary or another office independent of the drafter/sponsor, and §2.4 were limited to prospective classification, I could support the remedy.
